faq.answer: No. Training, temperament, sales duty, safety, or attraction norms may shape charisma. Compare the same task across focal, neutral, and anonymous audiences.
faq.question: Does charisma establish One-to-one Type Three?

faq.answer: Targeted presentation can be voluntary, rewarded, expected, or unsafe to refuse. Consent and evaluation power help separate strategic compliance from an inferred subtype pattern.
faq.question: Why record consent and power in this comparison?

faq.answer: Stable presentation across audiences, unchanged standards after a preferred person's disapproval, or appeal limited to paid work would weaken it.
faq.question: What weakens the persuasive-appeal hypothesis?

sections.body_md: The traditional description proposes that Type Three result attention may focus on being compelling to a particular person or pair. It is a prompt for comparison, not a claim about attraction as a cause.
sections.title: Treat persuasive appeal as a traditional hypothesis

sections.body_md: Compare the same pitch, performance, or collaboration for a preferred person, a neutral evaluator, and an anonymous audience. Record evidence, presentation, risk, reciprocity, and whether the result standard shifts.
sections.title: Match the task while changing the focal person

sections.body_md: One-to-one subtype language organizes observations about focal attention, appeal, and paired recognition. It is not evidence about bodily mechanisms, sexuality, chemistry, or a force that determines attraction or behavior.
sections.title: Keep one-to-one language non-mechanistic

sections.body_md: A person may emphasize a partner's success, a duo's image, or being the ideal collaborator rather than claiming individual credit. This variation must be compared with care, dependency, sponsorship, and role expectations.
sections.title: Allow partnership success to carry achievement

sections.body_md: Sales, entertainment, dating norms, client work, sponsorship, and appearance-based penalties reward targeted appeal. Record consent, power, economic stakes, safety, and who controls the evaluation.
sections.title: Test sales roles and attraction norms

sections.body_md: The hypothesis weakens when presentation remains stable across focal and anonymous audiences, a preferred person's disapproval does not alter the result standard, or targeted appeal appears only under a paid role.
sections.title: Use neutral audiences and consent changes as tests

sections.body_md: Findings tied to one measure and sample remain bounded to that instrument and context. This page cannot predict attraction, relationship quality, persuasion, sales performance, desirability, or compatibility.
sections.title: Keep appeal observations non-predictive

sections.body_md:
Duration: 5

Context: Choose one comparable task presented to a preferred person, a neutral evaluator, and an anonymous audience.

Observable signal: Record the result standard, evidence, presentation choices, reciprocity, consent, evaluation power, stakes, and response to disapproval.

Page-specific signal: Compare whether the focal person's reaction changes the definition of success while task evidence stays constant.

Alternative explanation: Compare sales duty, attraction norms, performance training, sponsorship, safety, economic stakes, and temperament.

Reflection prompt: Name the audience condition that most clearly disconfirms targeted appeal as a subtype modifier.

seo.description: One-to-one Type Three is a traditional, evidence-limited hypothesis that achievement attention may be expressed through persuasive appeal, admired partnership, or becoming compelling to a specific person. Charisma or appearance cannot establish subtype because sales roles, attraction norms, performance training, and unequal stakes can look the same.
seo.title: One-to-one Type Three: persuasive appeal as a matched-comparison hypothesis
